L339: ## 4 Generalization of older results
L340: 
L341: In this section we will explain why Theorem cite60†3.12 is a simultaneous generalization of three different results in the literature.
L342: 
L343: The congruence condition
L344: Theorem cite60†3.12 is proved in [cite32†26 , Theorem 4.4] under the additional assumption that S satisfies the congruence condition. To be precise, [cite32†26 , Theorem 4.4] is the simplified case given in Remark cite62†3.13 because in this case \(\mathcal {C}_{\bullet }(S)\) is a category by Corollary cite57†3.6 . This case includes inverse semigroups [cite24†28 ], semigroups of partial functions [cite33†21 ] and the Catalan monoid [cite37†19 ].

L346: Generalized matrix representations and strict right ample semigroups
L347: Let \(A_{1},\ldots ,A_{n}\) be algebras over a commutative unital ring \(\Bbbk \). For every \(1\le i,j\le n\) let \(A_{i,j}\) be an \((A_{i},A_{j})\)-bimodule where \(A_{i,i}=A_{i}\). Assume that for every triple (i, j, k) there exists an \((A_{i},A_{j})\)-bimodule homomorphism \(\Phi _{i,k}^{j}:A_{i,j}\otimes A_{j,k}\rightarrow A_{i,k}\) such that the associativity condition
L348: $$ \Phi _{i,l}^{k}\circ (\Phi _{i,k}^{j}\otimes {{\,\textrm{id}\,}}_{k,l})=\Phi _{i,l}^{j}\circ ({{\,\textrm{id}\,}}_{i,j}\otimes \Phi _{j,l}^{k}) $$
L349: 
L350: holds (here \({{\,\textrm{id}\,}}_{i,j}:A_{i,j}\rightarrow A_{i,j}\) is the identity function). The \(\Bbbk \)-module \(M[A_{i,j}]\) of all matrices
L351: 
L352: $$ \left( \begin{array}{cccc} a_{1} & a_{1,2} & \cdots & a_{1,n}\\ a_{2,1} & a_{2}\\ \vdots & & \ddots \\ a_{n,1} & & & a_{n} \end{array}\right) $$
L353: with \(a_{i}\in A_{i}\), \(a_{i,j}\in A_{i,j}\) is a \(\Bbbk \)-algebra with the obvious multiplication
L354: 
L355: $$ [M\cdot N]_{i,j}=\sum _{k=1}^{n}\Phi _{i,j}^{k}(M_{i,k}\otimes N_{k,j}). $$
L356: 
L357: If A is a \(\Bbbk \)-algebra, an isomorphism of \(\Bbbk \)-algebras \(\varphi :A\rightarrow M[A_{i,j}]\) is called a generalized matrix representation of A with degree n.
L358: We can restate Theorem cite60†3.12 in this language, at least when E is a finite set. Let S be a reduced E-Fountain semigroup which satisfies the generalized right ample condition and assume that \(E=\{e_{1},\ldots ,e_{n}\}\) is a finite set. Define \(A_{i,j}=\Bbbk _{0}\mathcal {C}(S)(e_{j},e_{i})\) where \(\Bbbk \) is any commutative unital ring. Note that \(A_{i}=\Bbbk _{0}\mathcal {C}(S)(e_{i},e_{i})\) is indeed a \(\Bbbk \)-algebra.
L359: Define \(\Phi _{i,k}^{j}:A_{i,j}\otimes A_{j,k}\rightarrow A_{i,k}\) on basis elements by
L360: $$\begin{aligned} \Phi _{i,k}^{j}(C(b)\otimes C(a))&=C(b)\cdot C(a) \end{aligned}$$
L361: 
L362: The associativity of \(\mathcal {C}(S)\) implies the associativity condition on \(M[A_{i,j}]\).
L363: 
L364: We can define \({\varphi :\Bbbk _{0}\mathcal {C}(S)\rightarrow M[A_{i,j}]}\) by setting
L365: 
L366: $$ [\varphi (C(s))]_{i,j}={\left\{ \begin{array}{ll} C(s) & e_{i}=s^{+},\quad e_{j}=s^{*}\\ 0 & \text {otherwise}. \end{array}\right. } $$
L367: It is clear that \(\varphi \) is a generalized matrix representation for \(\Bbbk _{0}\mathcal {C}(S)\) of degree |E|. Theorem cite60†3.12 now implies:
L368: ### Theorem 4.1
L369: 
L370: Let S be a reduced E-Fountain semigroup and let \(\Bbbk \) be a commutative unital ring. Assume that E is finite, S satisfies the generalized right ample condition and \(\trianglelefteq _{l}\) is contained in a partial order. Then \(\Bbbk S\) has a generalized matrix representation of degree |E|.
L371: This generalizes [cite28†10 , Theorem 3.2] which was proved for the class of strict right ample semigroups. A strict right ample semigroup S is a reduced E-Fountain semigroup (with \(E=E(S)\)) that satisfies stronger assumptions than the assumptions of Theorem cite63†4.1 . For instance, in a strict right ample semigroup the set E(S) is a commutative subsemigroup so \(ef=e\iff fe=e\) clearly holds and \(\trianglelefteq _{l}\) is a partial order.
L372: Moreover, the right ample condition \(ea=a(ea)^{*}\) holds and this is a stronger condition than the generalized right ample condition ([cite32†26 , Proposition 3.14]).
L373: Finite idempotent semigroups with central idempotents
L374: Let S be a finite idempotent semigroup with central idempotents. This means that \(S^{2}=S\) and \(ea=ae\) for every \(a\in S\) and \(e\in E(S)\). Setting \(E=E(S)\), it is shown in [cite39†30 , Section 6] that every \(s\in S\) has a left (right) identity from E. If \(e,f\in E\) are right identities of a then ef is also an idempotent and a right identity of a. Since \(ef\le e,f\) we deduce that every \(a\in S\) has a minimum right identity.
L375: Since E is central it is clear that \(ef=e\iff fe=e\) and \(e\in E\) is a right identity of s if and only if it is left identity of s. Therefore, S is a reduced E-Fountain semigroup with \(s^{+}=s^{*}\) for every \(s\in S\).
L376: ### Lemma 4.2
L377: 
L378: Let S be a reduced E-Fountain semigroup where the set E is central then S satisfies the generalized right ample condition.
L379: ### Proof
L380: 
L381: Assume \((ba)^{*}=a^{*}\) for \(a,b\in S\). We need to prove \((ba^{+})^{*}=a^{+}\) which is equivalent to \((ba^{*})^{*}=a^{*}\). Since \(ba^{*}a^{*}=ba^{*}\) it is clear that \((ba^{*})^{*}\le a^{*}\). On the other hand
L382: 
L383: $$ ba(ba^{*})^{*}=ba^{*}a(ba^{*})^{*}=ba^{*}(ba^{*})^{*}a=ba^{*}a=ba $$
L384: 
L385: so
L386: 
L387: $$ a^{*}=(ba)^{*}\le (ba^{*})^{*}. $$
L388: 
L389: Therefore \((ba^{*})^{*}=a^{*}\) as required. \(\square \)
L390: Since the set E is commutative the relation \(\trianglelefteq _{l}\) is a partial order. We have checked the requirements of Theorem cite60†3.12 so \(\Bbbk S\simeq \Bbbk _{0}\mathcal {C}(S)\) for every commutative unital ring \(\Bbbk \). In this special case, \(s^{+}=s^{*}\) for every \(s\in S\) so every non-zero morphism in \(\mathcal {C}(S)\) is an endomorphism.

L403: ## 5 Additional examples
L404: ### 5.1 The monoid of order-preserving functions
L405: Let \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {T}}\,}}_{n}\) be the monoid of all functions \(f:[n]\rightarrow [n]\) (where \([n]=\{1,\ldots ,n\}\)). A function \(f\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {T}}\,}}_{n}\) is called order-preserving if \(i\le j\implies f(i)\le f(j)\) for every \(i,j\in [n]\). We denote by \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) the submonoid of \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {T}}\,}}_{n}\) of all order-preserving functions.
L406: In this section we will see that \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) is a reduced E-Fountain semigroup that satisfies the generalized left ample condition so by the dual of Theorem cite60†3.12 there is an isomorphism \(\Bbbk {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\simeq \Bbbk _{0}\mathcal {C}({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n})\) of \(\Bbbk \)-algebras for any commutative unital ring \(\Bbbk \). We will also describe more explicitly the composition in \(\mathcal {C}({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n})\).
L407: Elementary observations
L408: 
L409: Recall that the kernel of of a function \(f\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) — \(\ker (f)\) — is the equivalence relation on its domain defined by \((i_{1},i_{2})\in \ker (f)\) if and only if \(f(i_{1})=f(i_{2})\). Since f is order-preserving, the kernel classes of f are intervals — if \(i_{1}\le i_{2}\le i_{3}\) and \((i_{1},i_{3})\in \ker (f)\) then \((i_{1},i_{2})\in \ker f\) also.
L410: Let \(K_{1},\ldots ,K_{l}\) be the kernel classes of f. Let \(y_{i}=f(K_{i}\)) and assume that the indices are arranged such that \(y_{1}<y_{2}<\cdots <y_{l}\). Choose \(x_{i}\) to be the maximal element of \(K_{i}\) and note that it must be the case that \(x_{l}=n\). Now, set
L411: 
L412: $$ X=\{x_{1},\ldots ,x_{l}\},\quad Y=\{y_{1},\ldots ,y_{l}\} $$
L413: so from every \(f\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) we can extract two sets \(X,Y\subseteq [n]\) such that \(|X|=|Y|\) and \(n\in X\). In the other direction, from two such sets \(X=\{x_{1},\ldots ,x_{l}\}\) where \(x_{l}=n\) and \({Y=\{y_{1},\ldots ,y_{l}\}}\) we can retrieve an f by setting
L414: 
L415: $$ f(x)={\left\{ \begin{array}{ll} y_{1} & x\le x_{1}\\ y_{i} & x_{i-1}<x\le x_{i}\quad (2\le i\le l). \end{array}\right. } $$
L416: As a conclusion, we observe that there is a one-to-one correspondence between functions \(f\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) and pairs of sets \(X,Y\subseteq [n]\) such that \(|X|=|Y|\) and \(n\in X\). From now on we denote by \(f_{Y,X}\) the function associated with \(X,Y\subseteq [n]\) (in contrary to [cite42†27 , Section 4.2] where this function was denoted \(f_{X,Y})\).
L417: Note that \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f_{Y,X})=Y\) (where \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f)\) is the image of f) and X contains the maximal elements of the kernel classes of \(f_{Y,X}\). Another easy observation is that \(f_{Z,Y}f_{Y,X}=f_{Z,X}\).
L418: The monoid \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) is a regular submonoid of \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {T}}\,}}_{n}\) and its Green’s equivalence relations are well-known (see [cite65†6 , Section 2]). In particular:
L419: $$\begin{aligned} f_{Y_{1},X_{1}}\,{{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {L}}\,}}\,f_{Y_{2},X_{2}}&\iff \ker (f_{Y_{1},X_{1}})=\ker (f_{Y_{2},X_{2}})\iff X_{1}=X_{2}\\ f_{Y_{1},X_{1}}\,{{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {R}}\,}}\,f_{Y_{2},X_{2}}&\iff {{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f_{Y_{1},X_{1}})={{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f_{Y_{2},X_{2}})\iff Y_{1}=Y_{2} \end{aligned}$$
L420: We want to define our distinguished set of idempotents E. Note that for every \(X\subseteq [n]\) with \(n\in X\) the function \(f_{X,X}\) is an idempotent that can be described by \(f_{X,X}(i)=\min \{x\in X\mid i\le x\}\). It will be convenient to define \(e_{X}=f_{X,X}\) where \(X\subseteq [n]\) with \(n\in X\) and we set \(E=\{e_{X}\mid n\in X\}\) (this is precisely the set of idempotents of the Catalan monoid — see [cite26†29 , Section 17.5.2]).
L421: We have just seen that \(f_{Y,X}{{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {L}}\,}}e_{X}\) and since \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {L}}\,}}\subseteq \widetilde{\mathcal {L}}_E\) we have \(f_{Y,X}\,\widetilde{\mathcal {L}}_E\,e_{X}\). On the other hand, it is not always true that \(f_{Y,X}\,{{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {R}}\,}}\,e_{Y}\) because \(e_{Y}\) is defined only if \(n\in Y\).
L422: Denote by \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal{O}\mathcal{F}}\,}}_{n}\) the submonoid of \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) of all order-preserving functions such that \(f(n)=n\) and note that \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal{O}\mathcal{F}}\,}}_{n}=\{f_{Y,X}\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\mid n\in Y\}\). This monoid was discussed in detail in [cite42†27 , Section 4.2]. We have \(f_{Y,X}\,{{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {R}}\,}}\,e_{Y}\) if only if \(f_{Y,X}\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal{O}\mathcal{F}}\,}}_{n}\).
L423: However, it is easy to see that
L424: $$ e_{Z}f_{Y,X}=f_{Y,X} $$
L425: if and only if \(Y\subseteq Z\). Therefore, the minimal left identity of \(f_{Y,X}\) from E is \(e_{Y\cup \{n\}}\) hence \(f_{Y,X}\,\widetilde{\mathcal {R}}_E\,e_{Y\cup \{n\}}\). It will be convenient to set \(\widetilde{Y}=Y\cup \{n\}\) for every \(Y\subseteq [n]\) so \(f_{Y,X}\,\widetilde{\mathcal {R}}_E\,e_{\widetilde{Y}}\) for every \(f_{Y,X}\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\).
L426: The first conclusion is that there exists an idempotent of E in every \(\widetilde{\mathcal {L}}_E\)-class and \(\widetilde{\mathcal {R}}_E\)-class of \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\). It is also easy to check that \(e_{Y}e_{X}=e_{X}\iff e_{X}e_{Y}=e_{X}\iff X\subseteq Y\) (see also [cite32†26 , Section 6] where we derived this fact from [cite66†2 , Lemma 3.6]) so \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) is a reduced E-Fountain semigroup.
L427: Since \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {L}}\,}}\subseteq \widetilde{\mathcal {L}}_E\) and there is a unique element of E in every \(\widetilde{\mathcal {L}}_E\)-class we deduce that \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {L}}\,}}=\widetilde{\mathcal {L}}_E\) and therefore \(\widetilde{\mathcal {L}}_E\) is a right congruence so \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) satisfies the right congruence condition.
L428: We will see later that \((f_{W,Z})^{*}=(f_{Y,X})^{+}\) does not always imply that \((f_{W,Z}f_{Y,X})^{+}=(f_{W,Z})^{+}\) so in view of Corollary cite57†3.6 we deduce that \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) does not satisfy the generalized right ample condition. However, it turns out that it satisfies the generalized left ample condition.
L429: Generalized left ample condition and isomorphism of algebras
L430: 
L431: First, we state the dual of the relevant results from Sect. cite41†3 . Every \(\widetilde{\mathcal {R}}_E\)-class of a reduced E-Fountain semigroup S is an incomplete right S-action and a partial function
L432: 
L433: $$ l_{a}:\widetilde{\mathcal {R}}_E(a^{*})\rightarrow \widetilde{\mathcal {R}}_E(a^{+}) $$
L434: 
L435: is defined by
L436: 
L437: $$ l_{a}(b)={\left\{ \begin{array}{ll} ab & (ab)^{+}=a^{+}\\ \text {undefined} & \text {otherwise}. \end{array}\right. } $$
L438: The dual of Proposition cite67†3.3 is:
L439: ### Proposition 5.1
L440: 
L441: Let S be a reduced E-Fountain semigroup. The following conditions are equivalent.
L442:

L446:

L450:

If we assume that \(\mathcal {C}(S)\) is a category and the relation \(\trianglelefteq _{r}\) is principally finite we can define a function \(\varphi :\Bbbk S\rightarrow \Bbbk _{0}\mathcal {C}(S)\) on basis elements by

L459: ### Theorem 5.2
L460: 
L461: Let S be a reduced E-Fountain semigroup and assume that \(\trianglelefteq _{r}\) is contained in a principally finite partial order. Then, the generalized left ample condition holds if and only if \(\mathcal {C}(S)\) is a category and \(\varphi \) is an isomorphism of \(\Bbbk \)-algebras.

L463: Next, we want to prove that \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) satisfies the generalized left ample condition.
L464: ### Lemma 5.3
L465: 
L466: Let \(f,g\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\). If \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(fg)={{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f)\) then \((f^{*}g)^{+}=f^{*}\).
L467: ### Proof
L468: 
L469: First note that \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(fg)={{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f)\) if and only if \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(g)\) intersects every kernel class of f. Now, \(\ker (f)=\ker (f^{*})\) so \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(fg)={{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f)\) implies that g intersects every kernel class of \(f^{*}\) and therefore \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f^{*}g)={{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f^{*})\). This implies
L470: 
L471: $$ (f^{*}g)^{+}=f^{*}. $$
L472: 
L473: \(\square \)
L474: ### Proposition 5.4
L475: 
L476: The monoid \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) satisfies the generalized left ample condition.
L477: ### Proof
L478: Let \(f,g\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) and assume \((fg)^{+}=f^{+}\). We need to prove \((f^{*}g)^{+}=f^{*}\). The fact that \((fg)^{+}=f^{+}\) implies that \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(fg)\cup \{n\}={{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f)\cup \{n\}\). Since \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(fg)\subseteq {{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f)\) we have two options. If \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(fg)={{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f)\) then \((f^{*}g)^{+}=f^{*}\) by Lemma cite68†5.3 . The only other option is
L479: $$ {{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(fg)={{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f)\backslash \{n\}. $$
L480: 
L481: In this case \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(g)\) intersects all the kernel classes of f except the kernel class of n. Since \(\ker (f)=\ker (f^{*})\), the image \({{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(g)\) intersects all the kernel classes of \(f^{*}\) except the kernel class of n. Therefore
L482: 
L483: $$ {{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f^{*}g)={{\,\mathrm{\textsf{im}}\,}}(f^{*})\backslash \{n\} $$
L484: which also implies \((f^{*}g)^{+}=f^{*}\) as required. \(\square \)

L486: We want to prove that \(\trianglelefteq _{r}\) on \({{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) is contained in a partial order. The following lemma will be useful.
L487: ### Lemma 5.5
L488: 
L489: Let \(f_{Y,X},f_{W,Z}\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\). If \(f_{Y,X}\trianglelefteq _{r}f_{W,Z}\) then \(X\subseteq Z\).
L490: ### Proof
L491: 
L492: The assumption that \(f_{Y,X}\trianglelefteq _{r}f_{W,Z}\) implies that
L493: 
L494: $$ f_{Y,X}=ef_{W,Z} $$
L495: 
L496: for some idempotent \(e\in E\). Recall that X is the set of all maximal elements of kernel classes of \(f_{Y,X}\) and note that \(x\ne n\) is a maximal element of a kernel class of \(f\in {{\,\mathrm{\mathcal {O}}\,}}_{n}\) if and only if \(f(x)\ne f(x+1)\). If \(f_{W,Z}(x)=f_{W,Z}(x+1)\) then
L497: 
L498: $$ f_{Y,X}(x)=ef_{W,Z}(x)=ef_{W,Z}(x+1)=f_{Y,X}(x+1). $$
L499: Therefore if \(x\ne n\) is a maximal element of a kernel class of \(f_{Y,X}\) then it is a maximal element of a kernel class of \(f_{W,Z}\). With the fact that \(n\in X,Z\) we deduce that \(X\subseteq Z\). \(\square \)
